hint_text: The empty body gives Verus no proof of the set equality. Prove it by set extensionality: for an arbitrary element x, show x is in (s1 + s2).map(f) exactly when x is in s1.map(f) + s2.map(f). Work one implication at a time. In each direction, make the membership hypothesis active with an explicit case split before eliminating the existential witness; otherwise choose cannot prove that the witness exists. For image membership, the witness is an a with a in s1 + s2 and f(a) == x; split on whether a lies in s1 or s2 to conclude membership in the corresponding image union. In the reverse direction, split on which image supplies the witness. Invoke the vstd set-extensionality mechanism by full path rather than adding a top-level import, because an added import can change generated Rust and fail the Lynette comparison. Check with run_verus after this, then run_lynette.

evidence_refs.observation: The empty function body fails the required postcondition.
A single direct membership equivalence assertion failed; SMT did not distribute the existential over union membership on its own.
Using choose under an implication without first case-splitting on the antecedent failed to prove witness existence.
Adding a top-level import for the extensionality macro made Lynette report 'Files are different'.
The final proof using full-path set extensionality and explicit case splits passed both Verus and Lynette.
